brief: A steel pipe flange. It is a disc 80 mm across and 10 mm thick, with a 30 mm bore through the centre. Four 8 mm bolt holes pass all the way through the disc, equally spaced on a 60 mm bolt circle. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

implied: The flange is made of steel.
stated: The flange is a disc 80 mm across and 10 mm thick.
It has a 30 mm bore through the center.
There are four 8 mm bolt holes pass all the way through the disc.
The bolt holes are equally spaced on a 60 mm bolt circle.
intent.summary: A steel pipe flange with a 80 mm diameter, 10 mm thickness, and a 30 mm bore through the center. It has four 8 mm bolt holes spaced 60 mm apart on a bolt circle. The flange carries no load.
unstated: The flange does not carry any load.

note: requirements: the record as the run accepted it, Forge's additions included; the bolt circle, which it did not carry, is added on parse. The answer is the designer's, returned identically twice: no bore, two 8 mm holes at the disc's centre and two 60 mm off its axis, all drilled sideways.

notes: dropped 1 load question(s): the brief states that this part carries no load, so there was nothing to be uncertain about
`feature_count:bolt_hole:primary` names no feature kind, so it was read as `feature_count:hole:bolt`.

added REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_X and REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_Y at 80 mm: the brief calls the part square or round at its largest stated size, and nothing in the requirement set measured the part's size at all. A dimension parameter is declared just as truthfully by a plate 30 by 12 as by a plate 30 by 30, and one was: sixteen claims, every one green, and the plate was 30 by 12.

added REQ_ROUND: the brief calls this part round, and two equal bounding boxes do not say a part is round -- a 25 mm square block has a 25 by 25 box exactly as a 25 mm cylinder does. One run asked for a shaft collar and got a square block with both extent claims passing. This measures the built surface: 1 is a cylinder, a square is 0.707.

added REQ_HOLES_30MM_ON_AXIS: the brief states 1 open hole of 30 mm down the part's axis, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

added REQ_HOLES_8MM: the brief states 4 open holes of 8 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.
not checked against 60 mm: the brief states it and no requirement carries it
